counters.src: PTI, police sources (ETV Bharat) 100+; Deccan Chronicle 200+; The Indian Express reported 60-70 in one batch at Connaught Place; no official figure for the day yet

counters.src: Outlook, citing officials in the evening; other figures differ: PTI (Business Standard) 3,000+, Reuters (Home Ministry official) 2,000+, ThePrint Hindi 3,500+, ABP News 4,500; in the afternoon police sources (ANI) had put it at about 1,000

items.h: CJP announces: the movement will now be nationwide, not just in Delhi; more than 200 detained on Sunday, 20 FIRs in two days

items.text: Report citing sources: Chief Justice Surya Kant declined to meet Rahul Gandhi and Kharge on 'vote theft'. It was said that no order can be passed at the administrative level, a petition should be filed on the judicial side, which may be heard on Tuesday. No official statement from the court yet.

Government and police side: according to DCP Neha Yadav, this group's earlier protests involved stone-pelting and arson, which is why Section 133 of the BNSS was imposed in several areas; Chief Minister Rekha Gupta praised the police, accusing the Congress, AAP, Left parties and the CJP of spreading anarchy. Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar compared the opposition to a cockroach crawling on one's back.

In Mumbai, Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Aaditya Thackeray stopped a police van carrying detained workers and warned that a Maharashtra bandh would be called if Shiv Sainiks were mistreated. Later, Aaditya and MNS's Amit Thackeray announced from outside Shivaji Park police station that the protesters held at Shivaji Park, Worli and nearby police stations had been released. The police's separate statement is not in this report.

items.h: 'Chalo Delhi, march for democracy' on Monday: from the Connaught Place-Barakhamba Road intersection to the Supreme Court at 1:30 pm; demands: stop vote theft, Gyanesh Kumar should resign, SIR should stop, ballot papers should return
Akhilesh Yadav, who did not join the previous two marches, is also expected to join the Supreme Court march; citing HT, the gathering was said to be at India Gate, while PTI said Connaught Place

items.text: SFI's allegation, in The Wire's report: 22 women activists from the tricolour rally at Connaught Place were detained after sunset, male policemen pushed and shoved them and they were taken in a bus without women police. The organisation calls this a violation of Sections 43(5) and 46(1) of the BNSS. The report does not carry Delhi Police's side, and there is no information yet on their release.

items.h: Mumbai: about 300 protesters detained at Shivaji Park, police say all released, FIR proceedings continue; Amit Thackeray said he had not seen such action even during the Emergency

items.text: SFI's claim, with a video on X: male policemen surrounded female students holding a tricolour rally at Connaught Place, and the bus they were taken in did not even have lights. Police's side has not yet come out.

Fresh detentions after 7 pm: according to SFI, Aishe Ghosh and other students of the organisation were detained again from Connaught Place; it alleges that male policemen misbehaved with the students during the tricolour yatra. According to ETV Bharat Hindi, people who had gathered to march towards Connaught Place were packed into buses, and a woman journalist was also picked up and later released.
items.src: ETV Bharat (English and Hindi live blogs)

items.text: At a press conference after his release, the CJP's Saurav Das alleged that Delhi Police entered Gurdwara Bangla Sahib during the action. He said a government that commits excesses in a gurdwara will not last long. Police have so far said nothing on this.

items.h: Vidya Krishnan in Al Jazeera: 'Modi is in trouble', calls 10 October only the first blow to the government

items.text: Rahul Gandhi's announcement: on Monday, opposition party leaders will march together to the Supreme Court and, by submitting a memorandum to the Chief Justice, demand Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, a halt to 'vote theft' and a stop to the SIR. He alleges that protesters were beaten by police and 'BJP goons'. These are Rahul Gandhi's allegations.

CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby alleged that during detention police injured MP John Brittas on the chest, and he was taken to RML Hospital for an X-ray. According to Baby, such excess was not seen even in the Emergency. Police response not yet received.

According to the CJP's Ajinkya Shinde, Mumbai Police detained protesters demanding Gyanesh Kumar's resignation at Shivaji Park and took them to the Worli police camp. He shared a video of the detention and wrote that you can catch us, you cannot silence us.

In Nagpur, Abhijeet Dipke sharply attacked Delhi Police: he alleges that even after telling him of his grandmother's death, he was not allowed two minutes with his brother or a lawyer, and was asked at 3:30 am to inform his parents of the arrest. He said the CJP will return to the streets. These are Dipke's allegations.

The picture by evening: hundreds of protesters advancing from Connaught Place's Inner Circle and Rajiv Chowk towards Jantar Mantar were detained. Unlike Saturday, trains, metro and buses ran as on normal days on Sunday, there was no internet curb and markets stayed open, though customers appeared few. Traffic was diverted on more than 30 routes leading to Jantar Mantar.

Aam Aadmi Party press conference: Sanjay Singh repeated the allegation of irregularities in the Haryana and Maharashtra elections and questioned the detention of CJP leaders; Gopal Rai said the movement will continue peacefully until Gyanesh Kumar resigns; Saurabh Bharadwaj condemned the remarks made on women protesters' clothing.

items.h: Dozens gathered at Mumbai's Shivaji Park in support of the CJP detained; activist Anjali Damania taken to an unknown location in a private vehicle by plainclothes policemen

items.text: The detained Neha Bora shared a video from inside a police bus and asked whether detention buses are now the new jails. According to her, the small glass-and-mesh compartments have no room even to breathe.

When Left organisations protested near RK Ashram Marg metro station, police detained everyone present. Reports say RAF, Delhi Police and CRPF personnel are clearing people from Connaught Place citing Section 163.

The international journalists' body CPJ said Delhi Police briefly detained at least six journalists reporting on the protest on Sunday, including journalists of The Indian Express and Hindustan Times. The CPJ asked police to honour the government's assurance in the Supreme Court that journalists would not be stopped.

Neha Bora's allegation: during detention, male protesters were abused over family, caste and religion and some were kicked; women were stuffed into small compartments in groups of six to eight. Police have not yet responded to these allegations.

Mallikarjun Kharge: even in the Emergency, trains and flights were not stopped. According to him, the government had arrests carried out to stop the protest, which shows that it fears the youth. He reiterated that the opposition will meet the Chief Justice on Monday.

Abhijeet Dipke wrote on X that he did not sign any bond promising not to protest and that he will take to the streets again. Saurav Das says the bond is only about not breaching the peace, and that peaceful protest is a constitutional right, not a breach of peace.
items.src: ETV Bharat (citing Dipke's and Das's X posts)

items.text: Reports citing sources say Delhi Police have sent fresh notices to CJP leaders in an old case in which a woman's photographs were allegedly doctored and circulated online. It is claimed the notices were sent after a High Court direction.

PTI: on the second day, more than 100 protesters advancing towards Jantar Mantar were detained, including students of SFI, AISA and KYS, and CJP supporters. Reports say several people were dragged and put into police buses. The CJP wrote on X that it will neither retreat nor be afraid.
NSUI's allegation: Delhi Police put up barricades outside its office and stopped national president Vinod Jakhar and other members from coming out.

items.h: Delhi Police's evening press conference: first official statement on the CJP protest, the detentions and the Supreme Court's directions

items.text: Neha Bora: the AISA president, with supporters, crossed barricades from RK Ashram Marg via Panchkuian Marg and reached Connaught Place, where police detained her again. She had also been detained from Dilli Haat on Saturday.

Opposition leaders erupted over the detention of CPI(M) MP John Brittas at Connaught Place: CPI(M) MP A.A. Rahim called it illegal and against the Constitution, CPI general secretary D. Raja demanded immediate release of all and no FIRs, Annie Raja said the movement will continue until the Chief Election Commissioner resigns. According to Navjivan, there was a heated argument between Brittas and police at the time of detention.

At a press conference, Saurav Das: the CJP will continue its protest against Gyanesh Kumar, 'we will not retreat', citizens should take to the streets. He alleges that party members' phones were taken without seizure memos and suspects that phones may be hacked or cloned to plant evidence. These are the CJP's claims; no response from police.

items.h: A protester running dressed as Gandhi, people escaping from police: viral videos of the CJP protest in one place

items.text: The other side: according to India TV's live blog, the BJP called Saturday's protest a 'flop show' and a defeat of mobocracy, and alleged that opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, are spreading anarchy at the behest of foreign forces. These are the BJP's allegations.

items.h: CJP alleges: leaders were 'kidnapped' from the aircraft, legal head Ratna Singh said the IB followed them from Bengaluru
The world's eyes on Delhi: how the Guardian, Reuters, AP, CNN, Le Monde and DW portrayed the detentions and the 'siege' of Delhi

items.text: Citing The Indian Express: about 60-70 protesters who advanced from Gate No. 6 of Palika Bazaar towards Connaught Place were detained, Sansad Marg closed. According to a senior police officer, if five or more people gather in the New Delhi area they will be detained. Police say four people seen beating a protester in a viral video have been identified and Kamla Market police station has taken suo motu action. DCP Sachin Sharma: the situation is under control. Meanwhile, the CJP's Jharkhand unit alleged that plainclothes men filmed and followed them at Ranchi station, so they cancelled coming to Delhi (unverified); Dhruv Rathee wrote that he accepted no bond or condition for his release.
items.src: Outlook live blog (citing Indian Express, ANI)

items.text: Details of the Supreme Court order: barricades across Delhi should be reviewed immediately; peaceful, unarmed crowds should not be detained without legal process, especially outside Section 163 areas; Section 163 notices around the court should be removed. The court clarified that the authorities' statutory powers will remain. Responses were sought on excessive force, illegal detention and the allegations about an officer without a badge. Next hearing on Tuesday.

On Sunday too, several protesters advancing from Connaught Place's Inner Circle and Rajiv Chowk towards Jantar Mantar were detained. According to police sources, they include CPI(M) MP John Brittas and members of student organisations, including SFI. SFI alleges that its all-India president Adarsh M. Saji was injured; police have said nothing on this.

CJP's press conference at the Press Club: Ashutosh Ranka said he was not detained but 'abducted' from the aircraft, and that the situation is worse than the Emergency. He alleges that Modi will protect Gyanesh Kumar at any cost, so the fight now goes beyond the Election Commission to the government. He also said police told Dipke of his grandmother's death in front of cameras, which was inhuman. No response from the government or police on these allegations.

items.h: After release, Abhijeet Dipke leaves for his village: on his grandmother's death said, the CJP will neither retreat nor be afraid

items.text: Leaving Kapil Sibal's house, Abhijeet Dipke said he is going to his family after his grandmother's passing; he criticised police for shutting down Delhi to protect Gyanesh Kumar. Delhi Police say they informed Dipke of his grandmother's death and offered help in reaching home, which he declined.
Abhijeet Dipke's video statement after release: going home because of his grandmother's death.

Police side: Delhi Police said on X that Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were arrested as a precaution under Sections 126 and 170 of the BNSS, all legal procedure was followed, and on Sunday they were produced before the SEM court in Delhi Cantt, where they were released on a bond to keep the peace for one year.

Supreme Court interim order: barricades in Delhi should be removed unless absolutely necessary; people should be allowed to move freely, the internet should be fully restored and lawyers should not be stopped from working. The metro should run on its normal timetable, restrictions only as legally permitted in the name of public order. DMRC must provide a map of the closed stations and the Centre must respond to all petitions.

items.h: Kharge announces: on Monday, India bloc MPs led by Rahul Gandhi on Delhi's streets, sought time to meet the Chief Justice

items.text: The court asked how a Section 163 BNSS prohibitory order was imposed right outside the Supreme Court; the Solicitor General said he had no instructions. The president of the Advocates-on-Record Association said lawyers were not even informed of the restriction. Justice Bagchi remarked that the lack of notice itself could be grounds to quash the order.

Senior advocate Sanjay Hegde, for the petitioners, alleged: lawyers who went to Sanjay Colony police station in Maidan Garhi on Saturday were held for hours and assaulted. Police have not yet responded.

Government side: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said there was no reduction in the total metro trips on 10 October, 271 trains ran per Saturday's normal timetable and movement was stopped at only 45 of 303 stations. According to him, most of those detained were picked up around 2 pm and released by 6 pm.

According to Delhi Police, a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was furnished for the release of Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das. Advocate Soutik Banerjee also confirmed the release. The CJP will now hold a press conference at 2 pm.

The Supreme Court (Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana) said that, per the earlier order, the officers accused of contempt must file a compliance report and reply by Tuesday. All intervention applications will be listed and a common order will follow. The habeas corpus petition will be heard later, in which Menaka Guruswamy sought interim relief citing about 7,000 detentions and 45 detention centres.

Both sides in court: senior advocate Shoeb Alam raised the issue of detention of people who came from outside Delhi and estimated 6,000 to 7,000 detentions. Counsel for the police officers said policemen were also attacked. The Solicitor General said he had not received the petitions; the petitioners say they were sent to his office.
CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka after release: we will hold a press conference at 2 pm.

items.h: CJP in Mumbai today too: appeal to gather at Shivaji Park at 4 pm, police step up deployment

items.text: Delhi Police and CRPF jointly carried out a flag march in Connaught Place's Inner Circle. Security was also stepped up on the Outer Circle.

In the Supreme Court, Kapil Sibal alleged that people were pulled off trains and detained, the internet was shut down and 45 metro stations were kept closed despite the court's order, and sought interim relief. One lawyer claimed he was grabbed and pushed into a moving bus. The court said the Solicitor General would also be heard.

The CJP's Ajinkya Shinde wrote on X that the government made a big mistake by detaining the leaders, and announced a protest at Mumbai's Shivaji Park (T Junction) at 4 pm. Mumbai Police registered an FIR at Gamdevi police station over Saturday's August Kranti Maidan protest; according to police, more than 400 people were detained there.

Delhi Police registered more than 20 FIRs over Saturday's attempts. The charges include disturbing law and order, obstructing government work and attacking policemen. Hearing on the contempt petition has begun in the Supreme Court.
Saturday's viral video: a protester dressed as Gandhi running away from police.
When police stopped him, a young man showed a doctor's prescription and said he was going for treatment.
Chaos in Connaught Place: a crowd of protesters ducked into a public toilet to evade police.
Scenes of the release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka after the court order

The Executive Magistrate's court ordered the release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. According to the CJP's legal head Ratna Singh, the condition is that the three keep the peace for one year. The three had been detained from inside the aircraft on arriving in Delhi on Saturday.

items.h: MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi: Kashmir-like conditions in Delhi, vote theft the biggest crime
The other side: Panchjanya called Saturday's attempt a failure, wrote that police and administration remain fully prepared today as well

items.text: Abhijeet Dipke's father said Delhi Police is lying; his mother alleged that her son was not even told of his grandmother's death.

At an event in Chennai, Rahul Gandhi called the Prime Minister 'Mogambo' and accused him of ruining democracy, and announced that on Monday the India bloc will take to the streets in Delhi again and the opposition will meet Chief Justice Surya Kant and demand action. In response, Union Minister Pralhad Joshi called it cheap rhetoric to hide political failure.

According to Republic Bharat, shops will stay shut in several areas today. The report also says protesters could not reach Jantar Mantar on Saturday, but small groups raised slogans at about 22 places.

Security was stepped up at Seva Teerth and Central Secretariat metro stations, with barricades in place. According to DMRC, the gates of all stations are open and the metro is running normally on Sunday.
According to Delhi Police sources, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was released at 3 am. The same sources say police will act again if protesters try to reach Jantar Mantar today.

items.h: Supreme Court's special sitting on a holiday: bench of Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana to hear contempt petition against the Home Secretary, Police Commissioner and DMRC chief over the metro shutdown and train cancellations

items.text: Delhi Police: Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurabh Das in preventive arrest, to be produced today before the Executive Magistrate at Delhi Cantt police station.

items.h: Four journalist bodies, including the Press Club of India, condemned the detention of journalists on reporting duty, said they were held even after showing press cards and phones and equipment were snatched

items.text: Extraordinary security in Delhi for the second day running: according to PTI, more than 30,000 police and paramilitary personnel deployed. Surveillance also tightened at railway stations and bus terminals.
Reports say the Congress has asked its MPs to stay in Delhi on Monday and the India bloc is preparing to submit a memorandum to the Chief Justice. Rahul Gandhi has announced a protest on 12 October.
At the Delhi-Noida border today, no paramilitary forces, only some Delhi Police personnel. Movement at Chilla border is normal.
According to sources, Dipke, Das and Ranka have been stopped as a precaution under Sections 107/151, with no formal arrest. The CJP's Ajinkya Shinde claims the three were not allowed to meet lawyers.
Some protesters began reaching Connaught Place; one said he has been there since yesterday. Police and paramilitary forces are deployed in the area, with warnings being issued over loudspeakers.
Sharing a Saturday video, condemned the alleged assault on a woman protester. Claims circulating on social media about the attackers' identity have not been verified.
RJD MP Manoj Jha filed a plea in the Supreme Court seeking urgent directions on the detention of protesters. The petition alleges use of force on unarmed protesters and closure of metro stations.
Dipke, Ranka and Das will be produced before the magistrate at 9 am; they will reach the police station with other lawyers.
Section 163 of the BNSS is in force around India Gate and Mandi House, with RAF and paramilitary forces deployed and warning boards put up. Roads are open.
Northern Railway: after two days of cancellations and rescheduling, all trains will run on schedule on Sunday.
Scenes of heavy police deployment and barricading at Jantar Mantar.

Delhi Traffic Police: from 6 am, diversions at 30 places depending on the situation, including Shankar Road, Dhaula Kuan flyover, Mandi House and Jantar Mantar Road. Those heading to stations or the airport should leave with time in hand; helpline 1095.

AISA president Neha Bora was released late on Saturday night. She had been picked up near the Safdarjung Airport flyover and held at the Maidan Garhi detention centre. After release she appealed to continue the protest today as well and to make every corner a Jantar Mantar.

The CJP's Ajinkya Shinde said the march towards Jantar Mantar will resume at 10 am and continue until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns. He told people to protest wherever police stop them.
